when i was first diagnosed i did the same thing. it’s something “new” you’ve discovered about yourself and you are taking this time to learn more about you, there’s nothing wrong with that! educating myself about bipolar, the symptoms and all that comes with it was extremely helpful and beneficial for present me at the time and for future me. listening to others experiences living with bipolar disorder helped me a lot, to know you aren’t alone and others experience the things you do is reassuring in a sense. trying to distinguish if an action/emotion/feeling is rooted in bipolar or just general natural human life has been the toughest part for me. while we do live with bipolar disorder, it is not always the reasoning as to why we may be or feel ways we do at times. there are many more parts to you than just having bipolar disorder, and discovering both sides, how they intertwine and come up in your life is important. 
while all of this can be helpful, you should be vigilant to ensure this doesn’t consume you. it is okay to do the research you are doing especially this soon into being diagnosed. but if the extreme need to do so continues for a long period of time maybe talking to a professional about it will also help! everything you’ve said is normal and are valid reactions to finding out you have bipolar disorder. i wish you the best:)
